name: TWIRX
mission: Reference implementation and public service of the Typed Web Commons
status_note: Live read-only Genesis baseline plus a published Opportunity Utility engineering release candidate. The large candidate runtime is not deployed; no arbitrary URLs.
footer_lead: TWIRX is the reference implementation and public service of the Typed Web Commons. Open protocol work for a verifiable, plural, and secure agentic Web. No token. No protocol ownership sold.

pages.title: TWIRX — A semantic highway for the Web
pages.description: TWIRX turns public web representations into reusable typed state with source-native values and verifiable provenance, so agents can query what a source represented without interpreting the same page again.

pages.heading: Query source-derived state. Trace every result.
pages.standfirst: Inspect the protected live baseline, a real historical delta, and the published million-packet Opportunity Utility engineering release candidate. Published evidence and deployed runtime state remain explicitly separate.
pages.title: Demo — query and trace the TWIRX Semantic Snapshot
pages.description: Inspect TWIRX's real RFC Editor archive delta, cross-origin materialized query, proof identities, and bounded local performance evidence.

pages.heading: From source bytes to a million-packet, proof-bearing Utility Universe.
pages.standfirst: E1 establishes the evidence kernel. Later gates add typed operations, Atlas admission, immutable semantic packets, a real historical delta, materialized views, and now a privacy-safe Opportunity release candidate. Every figure remains tied to a report or manifest.
pages.title: Proof — E1 through E4 evidence | TWIRX
pages.description: The complete TWIRX evidence record: source-statement fidelity, typed operations, Atlas admission, immutable packets and deltas, and the million-packet Opportunity Utility release candidate.

pages.heading: 500 selected origins. Three completed policy decisions. No inflated coverage claim.
pages.standfirst: The Atlas separates selection, policy, technical stage, publisher status, health, adapter trust and mapping trust. A selected identity is not a working adapter; only evidence-backed state contributes to public counters.
pages.title: Atlas — the 500-origin control plane | TWIRX
pages.description: The digest-verifiable Genesis Atlas: 500 selected identities, three completed human policy decisions, orthogonal origin state, and exact separation between selected, reviewed, observed, compiled and live.

pages.heading: Follow one value from origin bytes to typed result
pages.standfirst: Every panel on this page is generated from committed repository artefacts and re-verified at build time. Nothing here was typed in by hand, and the site refuses to build if the digest chain does not hold.
pages.title: Provenance explorer — one field, end to end | TWIRX
pages.description: An interactive trace of a single field through origin bytes, observation, content-addressed evidence, independent Go and C verification, native statement, declared transformation, and typed semantic result.

pages.heading: A compiler and trust architecture, not a browser wrapper
pages.standfirst: TWIRX separates observation, evidence, semantics, operational typing, execution, and authority so that no untrusted origin, adapter, model, or browser can silently become canonical truth.
pages.title: Architecture — planes, trust boundaries, and the slow/fast path | TWIRX
pages.description: The nine architectural planes of TWIRX, the E1 trust boundary, what each component is trusted to do, and the separation between the compilation path and the execution path.

pages.heading: Make your public information agent-readable without surrendering control.
pages.standfirst: TWIRX is designed to let publishers declare native terms, typed capabilities, attribution, access policy, refresh expectations, correction and revocation — with reverse engineering as a fallback, not the destination.
pages.title: Publish with TWIRX — publisher-controlled agent interfaces
pages.description: How publishers can prepare for TWIRX: preserve native vocabulary, declare read-only capabilities, retain attribution, and control correction and revocation.

pages.heading: Open protocol. Paid reliability. No pay-to-rank.
pages.standfirst: TWIRX can fund public infrastructure through hosted operation, sponsored open adapters, publisher-readiness work and private deployments without selling semantic authority or protocol governance.
pages.title: Economics — sustaining the open Semantic Data Plane
pages.description: TWIRX's sustainability model: sponsored open origins, hosted access, publisher readiness and private deployments, with no token or pay-to-rank.

pages.heading: Convert the verified kernel into a public, useful Semantic Highway.
pages.standfirst: The requested 90-day grant funds an executable ontology fabric, five useful semantic universes, a visual Atlas Agent, real change streams, publisher tooling, and a candidate-only semantic learning system.
pages.title: Roadmap — TWIRX's 90-day FUTO milestone plan
pages.description: The milestone-bound 90-day TWIRX plan: five Agent Utility Universes, an executable ontology, a visual agent, source-derived change streams, and a growing proof-linked corpus.

pages.heading: Shared meaning without semantic erasure
pages.standfirst: TWIRX does not replace a provider's vocabulary with a universal one. It preserves the native statement and adds a versioned interpretation whose context, evidence, and module closure remain visible.
pages.title: Semantics — native meaning, mappings as claims, governed canon | TWIRX
pages.description: How TWIRX keeps a provider's own term beside the shared semantic view, treats mappings as versioned claims, and separates open semantic extension from governed canonical admission.

pages.heading: Designed for hostile inputs, honest about current limits
pages.standfirst: TWIRX assumes an attacker may control the URL, DNS result, redirect, headers, body, JSON, adapter proposal, model input, or a contributor account. Every claim below states the boundary it applies to.
pages.title: Security — adversary model, current controls, and the gaps | TWIRX
pages.description: The TWIRX adversary model, the controls E1 actually implements, the residual risks that remain open, the production-deployment gate, and how to report a vulnerability.

pages.heading: Public protocol, practical Genesis stewardship
pages.standfirst: TWIRX is founder-led during Genesis because accountability requires a real decision-maker. That stewardship is constrained by a public charter and a published authority order.
pages.title: Governance — charter, authority order, and admission | TWIRX
pages.description: How TWIRX is governed during Genesis: the twelve founding laws, the decision classes and their required records, what funding cannot buy, and the conditions for distributing stewardship.

pages.heading: $30,000 for a 90-day Agent Utility Universe Alpha.
pages.standfirst: The first $6,000 milestone funds 30 days of focused engineering and public release work. The 90-day program expands the executable ontology, useful semantic universes, real source corpus, agent experience, change intelligence and publisher path.
pages.title: Funding — the TWIRX $30,000 FUTO milestone request
pages.description: TWIRX is requesting $30,000 for 90 days, beginning with a $6,000 public-release and full-time engineering milestone.

pages.heading: Progress is admitted through gates, not declared through ambition
pages.standfirst: The protected public baseline is live. A separate local E4 release candidate now adds 83,087 real Opportunity frames, more than one million source-derived packets and a bounded two-universe agent query; its remaining admission conditions are stated explicitly.
pages.title: Progress — the gate sequence and current state | TWIRX
pages.description: The TWIRX gate sequence from the founding architecture through the Semantic Data Plane Alpha, with the current state, evidence links, and admission condition for each gate.

pages.heading: The Web must remain open to every intelligence
pages.standfirst: A machine-readable Web will exist. The decisive question is whether it will be enclosed or shared, opaque or evidentiary, centralized or plural, persuasive or accountable.
pages.title: Manifesto — the public declaration | TWIRX
pages.description: The TWIRX public declaration, and how the declaration, manifesto, charter, and specifications divide the work of stating a commitment, a value, a law, and a technical contract.

pages.heading: TWIRX is an open Semantic Data Plane for the Web.
pages.standfirst: This page is the shortest path through the live protected baseline, the locally admitted Opportunity Utility release, exact scope, grant milestones, source, documentation and contact information.

pages.description: A concise FUTO reviewer path through TWIRX's working Semantic Snapshot proof, real archive delta, grant milestones, source, documentation and contact.
